database_name: F1 Verified Facts Project Memory Database

confidence_ladder.definition: Checked directly against an official FIA or Formula 1 source during database construction. Safe to state as fact and to cite.
A well-established record, consistently published in official sources over many years. Safe to rely on; cite the official archive if publishing.

Harvested from Wikipedia's season results tables, which are transcribed from FIA classifications. Every row was cross-checked on load against independently held season data. Reliable for results; not official under this database's policy, so cite the FIA/F1 archive if publishing.
Correct in substance. An exact figure or date may have drifted or may move with the current season. Confirm before publication.
Placeholder, disputed, or known to be incomplete. Never state as fact.

verification_policy.missing_fact_policy: Mark UNVERIFIED / NOT FOUND IN OFFICIAL SOURCES; never invent.
verification_policy.promotion_rule: Never promote a fact to 'verified' without an official FIA or Formula 1 source.
forbidden_as_authority: Fan sites, Reddit, secondary media, unsourced databases

source_registry.use: Primary authority for sporting, technical, financial and operational rules.
source_registry.licence: FIA copyright; published for reference, not redistribution.
source_registry.cadence: Reissued per season, amended in-season by WMSC decision.
source_registry.checkability: Nothing here outranks it. Its own numbers are checked against each other across seasons, and the limits it sets are stored in regulation_limits rather than on any car.

source_registry.use: Primary authority for FIA championship calendar, classifications and event status.
source_registry.checkability: The 2026 calendar it gives is checked against the stored race register on every build.

source_registry.use: Official Formula 1/FOM source for teams, drivers, cars, schedules, results and official explainers.
source_registry.checkability: Its career totals are reconciled against totals derived from the race records. That is what caught Russell's pole count and, before it, an internally inconsistent set of 2026 figures on the same pages.

source_registry.use: Official team facts, car names, power units, staff, bases and team history.
source_registry.checkability: Car names cross-check against the chassis register; nothing else here can contradict a team's own history page.

source_registry.use: Circuit/event facts; verify against FIA homologation where a technical or legal detail matters.
source_registry.checkability: Circuit length and turn counts are checked against the layout timelines, which must be complete and non-overlapping where present.

source_registry.use: Driver nationality, number, biography and career statistics.
source_registry.checkability: Every career win, pole and fastest-lap total is recomputed from the race records and compared.
The winner of every race is held independently from the Wikipedia harvest; the two must agree.

source_registry.use: Admitted as a REFERENCE source for race-by-race results only (see the 'reference' confidence tier). Its season tables are transcribed from FIA classifications and were cross-checked on load against independently held season data. Not admissible for narrative, attribution or contested claims, and never promoted to 'verified' without an FIA/F1 check.
source_registry.licence: CC BY-SA 4.0. Share-alike reaches any prose taken from it - see ATTRIBUTION.md.
source_registry.checkability: Race count per season, contiguous rounds, and every driver and constructor name resolving to the register. NOT sufficient on its own for standings grids: they left-pack their cells, a driver who missed a round shifts every later result a column, and the winner cross-check passes anyway because winners sit in the dense top rows. That route is closed.

source_registry.source: Fan sites, Reddit, secondary media, unsourced databases
source_registry.use: FORBIDDEN as authority under this database's verification policy. May be used to locate an official source, never to establish a fact.
source_registry.checkability: Nothing. That is the reason for the ban, not the size of the data.

source_registry.use: The chassis, engine, constructor and per-season entrant register: every chassis that has raced, and which constructor entered which chassis in which season. Loaded by tools/f1db_fetch.py. Its entrant mapping is the second, constraining source the chassis-per-race harvest was missing.
source_registry.licence: CC BY 4.0 - attribution only, no share-alike. The most permissive licence of any bulk source used here.
source_registry.cadence: Re-released after every race, versioned, with a public commit history and a changelog. Better maintained than anything else at this scale.
source_registry.checkability: Its (constructor, season) -> chassis mapping is checked against the 41 CAR_SEASONS assertions this database already held and had already proved against published win totals. Its chassis register is checked against the Wikipedia per-car articles for constructor and seasons. It carries NO technical specifications at all, so nothing it says can be mistaken for one.

source_registry.use: Chassis specifications: construction, suspension, engine, gearbox, brakes, weight, wheelbase, track, tyres, designers, predecessor and successor. There is no unified specification dataset for Formula One cars anywhere; this is where the data lives. Harvested by tools/wikispec_fetch.py.
source_registry.cadence: Continuous, by anyone; a historic car's article may not change for years, which for a fixed specification is a feature.
source_registry.checkability: Three checks, all of which must pass before a page is read at all: the constructor the infobox names must be the one F1DB gives the chassis; the years it reports must fall inside the seasons F1DB records it entered; and the article title must be a form of the chassis's own name. Afterwards its published win total is reconciled against the wins derived from this database's race records.

source_registry.use: The full race classification 1950-2026: every finisher and retirement with position, grid, laps, cause and points. Loaded by tools/ergast_load.py.
source_registry.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 on the Ergast data it continues: NON-COMMERCIAL. That is the most restrictive licence of any source here and it is the reason these rows are loaded locally rather than committed. The database dumps carry the same terms on their free tier; commercial use needs a supporter key.
source_registry.cadence: Per event, community-run, and explicitly a volunteer continuation after Ergast's shutdown - the least certain future of any source here.
source_registry.checkability: The winner it reports for a race must equal the winner already stored from the Wikipedia harvest or the race is refused whole; and the derived podium counts are reconciled against official career figures. That reconciliation is what caught a hand-relayed fabrication in v2.7, and it is what caught the loader's own resolver handing Wilson Fittipaldi's Brabham results to his brother Emerson on its first live run. The dump path is checked against the API path race by race (--verify-dump), because a second fetch implementation is a second place to be wrong.

source_registry.use: Car telemetry from 2023: speed, throttle, brake, RPM, gear and position at about 3.7 Hz, plus intervals, stints and radio. Free with no authentication for historical data; only real-time needs a subscription. NOT loaded: it covers 2023+ where FastF1 covers 2018+, and telemetry does not belong in this file at all.
source_registry.licence: MIT for the code; the underlying data is Formula One Management's.
source_registry.checkability: Its lap and stint data can be checked against FastF1's for the overlapping seasons, which is the only reason it would be worth adding. Nothing in this database constrains a telemetry sample.

source_registry.use: Per-lap timing, tyre stints, pit stops, race control messages and the team radio index, 2018 onwards. Loaded by tools/fastf1_load.py.
source_registry.licence: MIT for the library; the data is Formula One Management's and FastF1's guidance is personal, non-commercial use. Never committed here.
source_registry.cadence: Live during a session; nothing exists before 2018 and nothing will.
source_registry.checkability: Its finishing order is checked against the winner already stored, the same test the Jolpica loader applies.
